title: EvalRegistry
description: Canonical eval registry (HAR-97 CANONICAL EVAL STRATEGY section 12, HAR-140 / WP36): families E1-E22 and operational M1-M5, and per eval the surfaces (1-20) and dimensions it protects. An EVAL is a judgment on one episode, span or decision; metrics aggregate evals (metric_registry.v1.json); the completeness matrix (completeness_matrix.v1.json) refers to evals by id. The instance is contracts/evals/eval_registry.json.

gold_source.description: Where the reference answers the model judges are measured against come from: a different, stronger model, blind to the judge under test. They are NOT human labels, and every agreement figure and every surface that shows one says so (reference answers by a stronger model, not human).

buckets.description: The three canonical buckets, in order: context / organizational intelligence, decision / human judgment / action, system / eval health.

gates.description: The named gates of the buckets (B1-B9, D1-D10 in decision-flow order, S1-S5, and S6 for the efficiency metrics), each with the question it asks and what it improves or protects. A gate no eval is registered under yet (D6, D10) is shown as not measured, never as passing.

order.description: Position within the bucket: for Bucket 2 the step of the decision flow.

display_name.description: The short card name (HAR-97 v2 definitions). `name` stays the long registry name that the Go gate metadata and stored results pin.

display_question.description: The card question (HAR-97 v2 definitions). `question` stays the wording the stored results carry.

plain_what.description: HAR-149: what the gate does, in plain English for a non-engineer (the drawer's 'What are we doing?').

plain_why.description: HAR-149: the failure the gate catches and why it matters (the drawer's 'Why do we care?').

invariant.description: The bad behaviour the gate catches.

judges.description: The object it grades and the trace step.

grader.description: Who grades: deterministic code, a model, or both.

criteria.description: When each verdict applies, verbatim from the definitions. A verdict the definitions do not define for the gate is absent (never invented).

criteria_note.description: Free text the definitions give instead of per-verdict criteria (D6).

protects.description: What gets better because this gate exists.

when.description: The demo moment the gate runs at (Bucket 2 only in the definitions).

status_note.description: Bucket 3: what is built today, said honestly.

message.description: The Cliff Slack message of the one loop this gate judges (M1 what changed, M2 what to do, M3 what we learned from you, ecolite what is used next time); system for the S gates, which judge the machinery.

impact.description: What a failure of this gate changes in the backend today, read from the code paths and never inferred from the gate name.

impact_basis.description: The code citation that justifies impact.

mode.description: HAR-97 execution mode: live_required runs on every real episode that reaches the stage; live_conditional only when the trigger object exists (a missing prerequisite is never a pass); offline_benchmark runs on frozen cases and never on a live episode; continuous_aggregate is observability over many runs.

trigger.description: The Trigger / cadence column of HAR-97, verbatim.

not_triggered.description: For a live_conditional gate: the situation whose absence reads "Not triggered" (derived from `trigger`, never a pass).

control_effect_rules.description: HAR-149: the control effect each verdict of each gate has in the backend today, cited from code (never inferred from the gate name). `default` applies to a gate with no entry in `gates`; a gate entry overrides single verdicts and cites its code in `basis`.

only_for.description: The overrides apply only to results of this grader kind and these sub-gates.

known_deviations.description: Where an owner decision overrides the canonical text, recorded here rather than hidden.

bucket1_audit.description: Audit of the intelligence evals against Bucket 1 (HAR-97 B1-B9): per gate, the legacy E ids it maps, whether the existing implementation was correct with evidence (keep), judged the wrong object or passed without per-episode evidence (fix), or did not exist (missing), what was found and what the Bucket 1 builder added.

evals.description: E-family evals only: a judgment on one episode, span or decision. A hidden eval stays here (its owner and matrix cells keep it) but no surface lists or counts it.

metrics.description: The operational diagnostics M1-M5 (tokens, tool efficiency, eval overhead, latency, cost). They are metrics, never evals: they are not in evals[], are counted by no eval total and belong to no product area. An eval that was reclassified as a metric names its old id in reclassified_from.

job.description: Which of the three eval jobs the eval serves; follows the family's job.

bucket.description: context_intelligence: B1-B9. decision_action: D1-D10. system_health: S1-S6.

gate.description: B1-B9 (context), D1-D10 (decision flow), S1-S5 (system health), S6 (efficiency metrics, never evals).

judgedObject.description: What the eval judges: a contract type (PascalCase, a contract in contracts/schemas or a TraceSpan) and the field of that object that identifies it.

job.description: HAR-129 demo-loop clarification (2026-10-04): which of the three eval jobs the family serves. intelligence: context to trustworthy organizational intelligence (evidence fidelity, inference boundary, entity resolution, graph/state mutation, knowledge formation and applicability), shown with the business-intelligence update and the state diff. decision_loop: intelligence to decision, action, human feedback and updated knowledge (decision construction and ranking, action quality, human-judgment interpretation, edit propagation, knowledge mutation and later use). system: inward-facing engineering quality and efficiency (trace integrity, grader quality, reliability, safety, tokens, latency, cost), kept secondary in the operator view.

status.description: implemented: grader or metric code and gold on main. partial: a proxy, a unit-tested mechanism or a computable-but-unreported metric. planned: nothing on main, owned by a Linear issue (implemented_by may say "none (rebuild)" when an earlier pointer was wrong). hidden: out of scope for the current product loop; kept for its owner and the completeness matrix, never listed or counted by a surface.

contract_status.description: pending: the section 12 definitions (inputs, required trace fields, pass/warn/fail/unknown, failure modes, gold dataset) are written at the construction gate before implementation.

reclassified_from.description: On a metric: the E eval ids that were reclassified into it (a latency is a metric, not an eval).

area.description: The product area the eval is shown in (eval_areas.json): it follows the family's area.

also_gates.description: Further gates the eval also serves (a candidate's message is judged before the person chooses and again as the final one).

question.description: The question the eval's gate asks.

improves.description: What the eval's gate improves or protects.

legacy_id.description: The E id (or M id of a metric): kept as metadata for implementation compatibility; the product surface shows the gate, not this.

span_kind.description: The episode_trace span the eval's results attach to.

also_span_kinds.description: Further spans the eval attaches to (an action eval also runs on the final artifact at send).

demo_moment.description: Where in the demo the eval is exercised. M2: the chooser (three candidates). CES: choose, edit, send. M3: the judgment message (Correct, Edit interpretation, Do not learn this). ECOLITE: the second Play. OFFLINE: only against gold. LATER: later chronology.

required_trace_fields.description: Span ids and fields of contracts/traces/trace_schema.json the eval reads.

definitions_ref.description: Where the section 12 definitions of an implemented eval already live: eval types in contracts/evals/eval_catalog.json and the gold it is scored against.

allOf.description: A decision or feedback-loop eval (E8-E17) says what it judges, where and when. A hidden one is exempt.
